newsitem.title: GERMANY: IG Bau says sees slim chance for wage talk success.
newsitem.headline: IG Bau says sees slim chance for wage talk success.

text.p: The leader of Germany's IG Bau union said on Saturday he saw only a small chance for success in talks this week for some 1.3 million workers in the Germany's beleaguered construction industry.

IG Bau leader Klaus Wiesehuegel told journalists at a meeting in Bremen that the consensus model of reaching accord could collapse at the third round of construction industry wage negotiations in Frankfurt on Tuesday, March 25.

Wiesehuegel said construction employers were seeking to use the industry's high unemployment level to demand more flexible working conditions and reductions in bonus payments -- measures that IG Bau would reject.

Germany's construction industry has been suffering from recessionary conditions in recent months, hampered by a lack of demand for new projects and a bitter cold winter that kept many workers off job sites.

Wiesehuegel also criticised a decision by construction companies in Berlin and Brandenburg to back out of the talks, saying it was a bid to break the tradition of national talks in favour of regional wage discussions that the union is against.
